clue.text: Put roofs on some buildings, not this church

parts.note: the opposite of 'this' is 'that'

explanation.surface: Advice to roof some buildings but leave this particular church uncovered.
explanation.definitionFit: To thatch is to cover a roof with straw or reeds, as done on cottages and barns.

clue.text: Knitters recycled ornaments of little value

indicators.note: the letters are reused and made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People who knit turn old wool into cheap decorations.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinkets are small cheap ornaments or pieces of jewellery with little real worth.

clue.text: Some medicines rashly taken the wrong way that could poison people

indicators.note: the letters are read in the opposite direction, right to left
only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the run of letters sits across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A warning that pills swallowed carelessly could prove fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notorious toxic element, long the classic murderer's choice of lethal substance.

clue.text: Each year, in odd role, act tragic part

indicators.note: the yearly abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
odd means strange, so the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: An actor plays a strange role in a tragedy every year.
explanation.walkthrough: PA stands for per annum, Latin for 'by the year'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra is the title heroine of Shakespeare's tragedy Antony and Cleopatra, a famous stage role.

clue.text: Letters inside thin cover that could be extra weight

parts.note: the two letters between the ends of 'thin' are H and I, written out as 'H and I'
a cap is a covering, as for the head or a bottle

explanation.surface: Something about letters slipped inside a thin cover that adds weight to a package.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner letters of 'thin' are H and I, and the clue wants that phrase spelt out in full, 'and' included.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing a handicap is the extra weight a stronger horse must carry to even the field.

clue.text: Article annoyed executives collectively and uniformly

parts.note: cross means angry or irritated
the directors of a company together form the board

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece angered the bosses, all of them equally.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying across the board means affecting every part or member equally, without exception.

clue.text: After protest, bishop put out of service

indicators.note: the bishop follows on from the protest

parts.note: demo is short for demonstration, a public protest

explanation.surface: A bishop is defrocked after joining a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the chess notation for bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To demob is to release someone from military duty, short for demobilise.

clue.text: Informal talk over French drink in fine house there

indicators.note: in a down clue the talk sits above the drink

parts.note: a chat is a casual conversation
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A cosy chat over a French glass of something in a grand home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to France, so the definition is a French grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country mansion, the grand residence of the gentry.

clue.text: Colours are not used in added text

indicators.note: the informal negative is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PS is the postscript added at the end of a letter
ain't is an informal form of are not

explanation.surface: A note that certain colours weren't used, added at the end of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something is to apply colour to it, so paints and colours are both verbs here.

clue.text: Routine transactions strangers did no differently

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a different way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strangers handled everyday business in an unusual manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A standing order is a regular bank instruction to pay a fixed sum on fixed dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing orders are instructions to a bank to make a regular, repeated payment automatically.

clue.text: Half-hearted copper isn't potentially this?

indicators.note: what the letters could potentially become, once rearranged
the doubled letter at the heart of 'copper' is halved, losing one of the pair

parts.note: taken as written before its doubled middle letter is halved
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A lukewarm policeman might never rise to a senior rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a half-hearted copper is not likely to become a senior detective.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police rank above sergeant, the kind of promotion an ambitious copper aims for.

clue.text: US city in which the writer is turned back — is that so?

indicators.note: the contraction for the writer's 'I am' is read from right to left

parts.note: the setter says 'I am', shortened to I'M
'Am I?' is a doubtful reply meaning 'is that so?'

explanation.surface: A writer wonders aloud about turning back in some American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Am I?' is said in reply to a remark one doubts, much like 'is that so?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a major city on the Florida coast in the United States.

clue.text: Key member of group appearing in shocking pink

indicators.note: the answer shows itself within the letters of the following words

parts.note: taken as written; the answer runs across the two words

explanation.surface: The star of a band shows up dressed in shocking pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking pink' is a vivid colour name that reads naturally, which disguises the letters sitting across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the most important person in an organisation, the one everything depends on.

clue.text: Discipline citizen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a field of study, such as history or physics
second meaning: a person owing allegiance to a state or monarch

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the two words look like an instruction to punish a member of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an academic area of study and a person who is under a sovereign's rule.

clue.text: It's not put in speech one delivered in first part of the performance

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

indicators.note: the numeral is handed over into the middle of the following letters

parts.note: an act is a turn or performance on stage

explanation.surface: Something left unsaid, like a line skipped in the first act of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First part of the performance' looks like Act One, but 'first part of' takes only the initial of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being stated out loud in words.

clue.text: Create interest in plot

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to arouse someone's curiosity
second meaning: a secret scheme or conspiracy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a writer's tip about making a story's plot gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means fascinate; as a noun it means scheming or a secret plan.

clue.text: Job description he might have given, being restless

wordplay.words: Job description he might have given
wordplay.note: Job, the biblical man famed for patience

explanation.surface: Someone fidgety while describing their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work, but it is the long-suffering figure of the Old Testament; split the answer 2,7 to hear him.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impatient means being restless and unwilling to wait calmly.

clue.text: Minimal change in broadcast shown again

indicators.note: the small coin is put inside the word for broadcast

parts.note: relayed means transmitted, as by radio or television
p, a penny, is the smallest unit of British change

explanation.surface: A broadcast with a tiny edit was aired a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something replayed is played or screened once more, like a repeat of a match or programme.

clue.text: Novice driver taken in by unusual throttle or choke

indicators.note: the learner is swallowed up inside the word for unusual

parts.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary
L is the learner plate on a British novice's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver confused by an odd throttle or choke on the car.
explanation.walkthrough: Throttle and choke look like car controls a learner might fumble with, but here they are verbs for squeezing a throat.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle is to squeeze the neck to stop breathing, the same act as throttling.

clue.text: American's carrying nothing within London area

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the word for carrying

parts.note: tote is an American word for carry
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An American carrying nothing around a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: TOOTING is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooting is a residential district in the south London borough of Wandsworth.

clue.text: Legal support group sheriff initially put in position

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the word for a position

parts.note: a pose is a posture or stance

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A sheriff first sets up his band of helpers in a strategic spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of citizens summoned by a sheriff to help enforce the law.

clue.text: Satirical writer left on journey, finally, with expedition

parts.note: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: only its closing letter is used

explanation.surface: A satirist sets off on a journey as part of an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, but here it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, so acting with it means acting quickly.

clue.text: Transform cast, or its make-up

definitions.note: plural people who make up a cast, referred to by what the cast consists of

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director told to change the cast, or at least its stage make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests greasepaint, but it means composition: what a cast is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical cast consists of performers, so they form its membership.

clue.text: Aircraft made of metal gaining height after start

indicators.note: the metal takes on an extra letter
the added letter goes just after the first letter of the metal

parts.note: copper is a reddish metal

explanation.surface: A plane built of metal climbs once it has taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper is the informal word for a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is slang for a helicopter, a rotor-driven flying machine.

clue.text: Young boxer, say, framing popular photograph of actress

indicators.note: the young dog surrounds the word for popular like a frame

parts.note: a boxer is a dog breed, and a young dog is a pup
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A young fighter posing in a frame beside a popular starlet's picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter but is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a picture of a glamorous star pinned on a wall by an admirer.

clue.text: To a liner out East — at sea, or in dock

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the compass point is taken out of the words

parts.note: taken as written, before the compass letter goes

explanation.surface: A ship heading East, either sailing on the ocean or moored in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In dock' here means in the courtroom dock, the place where an accused person stands, not a harbour berth.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant standing in the dock is being tried before a court.

clue.text: Bulb repeatedly lit, absorbing current

indicators.note: taking in, so the current goes inside the doubled word
the word for lit is given more than once, here twice

parts.note: a light that is lit is on
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A light bulb is switched on again and again, drawing current each time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' looks like a light bulb but is the vegetable; ONON takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a bulb, the underground storage organ of a plant, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Treehouse put in ahead of time, with serious intent

indicators.note: the treehouse is placed inside the word for ahead of time

parts.note: early means before the expected time
a bird's nest is literally a house up a tree

explanation.surface: A treehouse built well in advance by someone who meant business.
explanation.walkthrough: A treehouse here is a bird's home in the branches, not a child's den.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means sincerely and with deep conviction, as when doing something with purpose.

clue.text: Finalise contents of out-tray? It provides guidance, by the way

definitions.text: It provides guidance, by the way

parts.note: to sign a letter is to complete it before sending
the out-tray holds outgoing post or mail

explanation.surface: Clearing the office out-tray, with a guide to show the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' is both a throwaway phrase and literally 'beside the road', where such things stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost stands at the roadside and shows travellers which direction leads where.

clue.text: Didn't go steady, switched around (apart from first couple)

indicators.note: the letters are swapped into a new order
the first two letters stay in place; only the rest are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; its letters after the first two are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple who stopped going steady, with things reversed apart from the first pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go steady' looks like the dating phrase, but 'Didn't go' is the definition and 'steady' is the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Stayed means remained in place, the opposite of leaving or departing.
